title: the Yaksha's questions
hook: one brother may live: Yudhishthira chooses Nakula, and the yaksha shows who he really is
carry: the one who keeps the family fair

segments.voice: Yesterday: dharma, the right way, hidden as if in a cave, and the wonder that we live as if we'll never die. Your line was a modest supper under your own roof.

The questions are over, and the yaksha is satisfied. One of your brothers may live, he says. Choose. On the shore lie four of them. Bhima, whose strength the family leans on. Arjuna, the archer they'll need in any war to come. And the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva. Yudhishthira looks at them all, one by one, for a long moment. Then he names one, and the yaksha asks him why.
screen: `ONE BROTHER MAY LIVE.` → `FOUR ON THE SHORE.` → `CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: Let Nakula live, Yudhishthira says. Why him? Why not Bhima, so strong, or Arjuna, whom you all depend on? Yudhishthira's answer is about fairness. My father had two wives, Kunti and Madri. I am Kunti's son, and I'm alive. Let Madri have a living son too. He passes over the brothers who could win him a war, and chooses the one who keeps the family fair. The yaksha is delighted. Because you hold harmlessness higher than gain or pleasure, he says, let all four of your brothers live. And they stand up, as if from sleep, their thirst gone. Then the stranger shows his face. He is Dharma himself, Yudhishthira's own father. He came to see his son, and to test him. The deer that ran off with the fire-sticks was Dharma too. So the whole day, the chase, the thirst, the lake, the questions, was a father asking his son: do you know what dharma asks of you? Dharma offers him gifts. Yudhishthira asks first for the brahmin's fire-sticks back, the errand that started it all. Then that in the coming year in hiding, no one will recognize the brothers. And he asks to conquer greed, anger and folly, and to keep his mind on generosity, truth and self-discipline. Dharma grants it all. The Pandavas walk back to camp with the fire-sticks in hand, and ahead of them waits a year in disguise.
screen: `LET NAKULA LIVE.` · `A LIVING SON FOR MADRI TOO.` · `THE YAKSHA IS DHARMA, HIS FATHER.` · then, large: `ALL FOUR STAND UP.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a group you belong to, a family, a team, a circle of friends, and look for the person in it who is easiest to overlook, the one without a loud voice on their side. Hold them in mind the way Yudhishthira holds Madri's sons in mind, and with each breath wish them well. If you pray, you can bring them into your prayer.
Dharma, the god who stood at the lake all along, revealed at last as Yudhishthira's own father. A test by a lake that ends with a fair choice, and four brothers alive. Today's word.
Your line: the one who keeps the family fair. A living son for each mother, and four brothers standing. Day eight hundred six, done.

screen: `DAY 806 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.`

chat.says: Why did Yudhishthira pick Nakula to live instead of strong Bhima or Arjuna?
options: So his father's other wife, Madri, would have a living son too. It was fair.
Nakula was closest to the lake, so he could be saved fastest of the four.
He thought Nakula knew the answers to the yaksha's remaining riddles.
chat.meaning: Yudhishthira, Kunti's son, is alive, so he asks for Madri's son Nakula: a living son for each mother. Pleased, the yaksha restores all four.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), the end of the episode of the Yaksha's questions: the choice of Nakula; the brothers restored; the yaksha revealed as Dharma; the boons

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Yudhishthira chooses Nakula; the yaksha asks why not Bhima or Arjuna; his reasoning about Kunti and Madri; the yaksha restores all four because he values harmlessness/fairness above profit.

Confirm Dharma's self-revelation as Yudhishthira's father, that he took the form of the deer, and the boons: the arani returned; the Pandavas unrecognized during the year in hiding; Yudhishthira's wish to conquer covetousness, folly and anger and to be devoted to charity, truth and asceticism.
'A father asking his son: do you know what dharma asks of you?' is an interpretive line, not the text's.
Ganguli has the yaksha's reason as Yudhishthira regarding harmlessness (or not being cruel) above profit/pleasure; 'fairness above advantage' is a paraphrase. Confirm.

Editor pass: the yaksha's stated reason now follows Ganguli (harmlessness above gain and pleasure) instead of 'fairness above advantage', in the teach, screen and fork reveal; Yudhishthira's own reasoning (a son for each mother) is still framed as fairness. Cut 'the youngest' (superlative not in the cited text), the templated 'Today, ...' hook closer, the 'greatest wonder' and 'last four' carry-overs from 805, and the howItsDone claim that the choice 'is retold as the heart of the episode'.

Audit: the teach repeated the hook's 'the yaksha, puzzled' in its first lines; trimmed. Facts (Nakula, Kunti/Madri, harmlessness above profit and pleasure, Dharma as the deer, the three boons) match Ganguli.
